name: Paris
notes:
LitArbi 0.9.74-beta “Paris” (build 84): pinpoints in the matter's language.
• Citations write their page and paragraph signs as the matter does: "Beilage 3, S. 4, Rz. 12" in a Swiss matter, "Anlage K 1, S. 4, Rn. 12" in a matter from Germany — the page first, as Swiss and German briefs cite — and "par." and "p." in French, "párr." in Spanish, "parág." in Portuguese. This holds where a template says "¶" and "p.", when Update Exhibits rewrites a citation, for a submission cited by its name, in cross-references to your own paragraphs and in the index of authorities.
• Several pages keep the language's own sign: "pp." in English, Spanish and Portuguese; "S." in German and "p." in French.
• With the exhibit number placed after the description, the number now also comes before a Portuguese or Malay pinpoint.
Windows 10 (1809) or later, x64 or ARM64.
